title: 2002 AMC 12B Problem 21
statement: For all positive integers \(n\) less than \(2002,\) let \[a_n=\begin{cases} 11, & \text{if } n \text{ is divisible by } 13 \text{ and } 14;\\ 13, & \text{if } n \text{ is divisible by } 14 \text{ and } 11;\\ 14, & \text{if } n \text{ is divisible by } 11 \text{ and } 13;\\ 0, & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases}\] Calculate \(\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{2001} a_n.\)

solutions.text:
Since \(2002=11\cdot13\cdot14\) with \(11,\) \(13,\) \(14\) pairwise coprime, \(a_n=11\) when \(n\) is divisible by \(182,\) \(a_n=13\) when \(n\) is divisible by \(154,\) and \(a_n=14\) when \(n\) is divisible by \(143\) (and no \(n\lt2002\) is divisible by all three).

For \(n\le2001\) there are \(10\) multiples of \(182,\) \(12\) of \(154,\) and \(13\) of \(143.\) So the sum is \[ \begin{gathered} 11\cdot10+13\cdot12+14\cdot13 \\ {}=110+156+182 \\ {}=448. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Because \(11,\) \(13,\) \(14\) are pairwise coprime, “divisible by two of them” means divisible by their product
